ravi (Docs): Heads-up: I opened a PR that tries to reconcile timeout vs 429 guidance for streaming calls and adds a small SDK helper for safe cancel+retry with context trimming. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5011

emily (SRE): nice. can you call out the scenario we keep seeing: client cancels a streaming call after partial tokens and immediately retries, causing a second spike and more 429s. we should advise a backoff + jitter on cancel paths.

ravi (Docs): yes — added a short note recommending a cancellation cooldown and showing how to include the partial buffer when trimming. Also included a curl reproduction for local testing.

noah (SDK): can the helper be small and opinionated? e.g., cap concurrent retries per user, honor Retry-After header, and prefer summarization when >75% tokens trimmed. i can author the JS/py snippets.

ravi (Docs): perfect. i added a placeholder snippet section — please replace with SDK final.

frida (Eng): ops caveat: when clients cancel TCP streams, the server may still bill for tokens already generated; add a line advising clients to account for potential token duplication in cost estimates.

emily (SRE): also add a link to the ticket where we measured dedicated vs hosted Retry-After distributions: https://internal.redwood/tickets/rl-6722 so customers can see expected values.

ravi (Docs): linked the ticket and added a small table summarizing typical Retry-After ranges for hosted/dedicated.

noah (SDK): pushing a JS streaming helper now. gist in PR shows:```js
// safe-retry-stream.js (snippet)
const {tokenize} = require('@redwood/tokenizer')
async function safeRetryStream(client, req, maxTokens, opts = {}) {
  const {maxAttempts = 4, jitter = 0.2, maxConcurrentRetries = 2} = opts
  let attempts = 0
  let concurrentRetries = 0
  while (attempts < maxAttempts) {
    const resp = await client.stream(req)
    if (resp.ok) return resp
    const ra = parseFloat(resp.headers.get('Retry-After') || '0')
    const wait = ra > 0 ? ra : (Math.pow(2, attempts) * (0.5 + Math.random() * jitter))
    // include partial buffer as tokens when trimming
    const partialTokens = tokenize(resp.partial || '').length
    req.messages = trimForTokens(req.messages, maxTokens - partialTokens)
    attempts += 1
    concurrentRetries = Math.max(0, concurrentRetries - 1)
    if (concurrentRetries >= maxConcurrentRetries) throw new Error('too many concurrent retries')
    await sleep(wait * 1000)
  }
  throw new Error('exhausted retries')
}
```

ravi (Docs): awesome. added a callout to prefer summarization when the doc says fidelity matters. also wrote a tiny Python backoff snippet for non-streaming.

noah (SDK): pushed a small change: use Retry-After precedence, but if it's <0.5s treat it as a soft hint and still add jitter to avoid synchronization. also added a comment about token-count differences across model families.

frida (Eng): small wording nit: under "cost impact" say "may incur duplicate partial tokens" instead of "double billing". less alarmist.

emily (SRE): nit: the curl repro should include a header save so folks can post samples to support. i suggested:
```bash
for i in {1..300}; do curl -si -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | sed -n '1,30p' >> /tmp/429-sample.txt; sleep 0.03; done
```

ravi (Docs): updated curl example and adjusted the cost wording per frida.

merge-bot: ravi updated files: docs/troubleshooting/streaming-cancel-retry.md, snippets/safe-retry-stream.js, snippets/backoff_nonstream_py.py

ravi (Docs): asking for quick reviews @emily @noah so this can land in the next docs deploy. anything else we should add (runbook anchor, admin note)?

emily (SRE): ack, i'll double-check the dedicated Retry-After numbers tomorrow and confirm the runbook anchor /tickets.

noah (SDK): ack from SDK, verified snippets run lint + added tokenizer import path. good to merge.
